title: Images of invariant boundary components are Q-Cartier
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth] with an admissible tame action of a finite group $G$: invariant affine opens cover $X$ and each geometric inertia has order invertible at the point. Let $B\subseteq\overline B$ be invariant strict normal crossings divisors [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] and assume the divisorial log scheme $(X,\overline B)$ is very tame [def-per-very-tame-divisorial-action], with its fs log structure as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Let $q:X\to Y=X/G$ be the finite quotient. The image $D=q(B)$ is the support of an effective Q-Cartier Weil divisor: etale locally on $Y$ there is a non-zero-divisor $c$ whose zero set is exactly $D$. Here an effective Q-Cartier divisor means an effective Weil divisor some positive multiple of which is locally principal, and a Weil divisor on a normal Noetherian scheme is a finite integral combination of integral codimension-one closed subschemes. If $h:Y'\to Y$ is a birational modification with $Y'$ regular such that $(h^{-1}q(\overline B))_{\rm red}$ is a normal crossings divisor, then $(h^{-1}D)_{\rm red}$ is a union of its components and is normal crossings. It is strict normal crossings whenever the ambient divisor is strict normal crossings.

At a strict local point, write $H$ for inertia, $N=|H|$, and suppose the roots of unity of order $N$ have been adjoined. There is a local equation $b$ for $B$ which is an $H$-eigenvector and $b^N$ is invariant. Its image in the invariant local ring cuts out a Cartier divisor with support $D$.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, printed p.125, middle paragraph, using the eigenparameter averaging of Lemma 5.3.5; VIII 5.4.1 identifies the strict local invariant quotient.

proof.text: Fix $\bar y$ and a geometric lift $\bar x$. Put $H=\operatorname{Stab}_G(\bar x)$, $N=|H|$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $R=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$. The finite quotient and log stalk statement [lem-per-finite-quotient-strict-local-invariants] gives $R=A^H\hookrightarrow A$, a finite extension, and Noetherian $Y$. By [lem-per-regular-boundary-divisorial-chart] applied to $\overline B$, the log structure is fs and its sharp monoid at $\bar x$ is $\mathbf N^r$, with generators giving regular parameters. Regularity of $A$ follows from [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular]. Its prime localizations are regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal] makes $A$ normal. If $z\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ is integral over $R$, it is integral over $A$, hence belongs to $A$; it is $H$-fixed, hence in $R$. Thus $R$ is a normal local domain. The local map $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to R$ is faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat]; [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-normal-ring-descent] shows $Y$ normal. Since $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is Noetherian, so is its strict henselization $R$ [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian].

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, printed p.125, Q-Cartier paragraph; VI 3.5(a), 3.7(a), printed pp.74–75, for the equivariant chart.

proof.text: Very tameness means in particular that $N$ is invertible and $H$ fixes the characteristic monoid [def-per-very-tame-divisorial-action]. Apply [lem-per-very-tame-equivariant-sharp-chart] with $Q=\mathbf N^r$. Write $t_i=a(e_i)$ for the images in $A$ of its generators; compared with the regular-boundary chart of Step 1 these change only by units. Hence they remain regular parameters. Each $t_i$ is an eigenvector $h(t_i)=\chi_i(h)t_i$ with $\chi_i(h)^N=1$, and these roots are $H$-fixed. Since $B\subseteq\overline B$ is a reduced Cartier divisor, its local equation becomes a unit after inverting $T=\prod_{i=1}^r t_i$. By [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] that equation is $u\prod_i t_i^{d_i}$; The ring $A/(\text{equation})$ is the filtered colimit of the local rings of $B\times_XW$ over pointed etale neighbourhoods $W$, which are reduced by [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent]; so it is reduced, and this forces $d_i\in\{0,1\}$ (a prime power of exponent at least two gives a nonzero nilpotent class). Let $S=\{i:d_i=1\}$ and $b=\prod_{i\in S}t_i$. Then $b$ generates the ideal of $B$ in $A$, is an eigenvector with character $\prod_{i\in S}\chi_i$, and $b^N\in R$. Empty $S$ gives $b=1$.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, printed p.125, Q-Cartier paragraph; VI 3.5(a), 3.7(a), printed pp.74–75, for the equivariant chart.

proof.text: We will compare codimension one upstairs and downstairs. The extension $R\hookrightarrow A$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability] contraction sends any strict prime chain in $A$ to a strict chain in $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-going-down-normal-integral], every chain ending at the contraction of $P\subset A$ lifts to one ending at $P$. Consequently the two heights agree. Every height-one prime of $R$ has a prime above it by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over], necessarily of height one. By [rem-pc-regular-normal], normal Noetherian schemes have disjoint open-and-closed integral components. The saturation of a source component under $G$ is clopen, so its orbit-space image is a clopen integral component of $Y$. Restrict source and target to these components when applying the same chain argument on invariant affine quotient charts from [lem-per-admissible-quotient-affine-integral-charts], using normality of $Y$ and $X$: each image of a component of $B$ has codimension one. Thus the reduced image determines the effective Weil divisor $E=\sum_{Z\text{ component of }D}[Z]$. Under strict localization its support is the image of $V(b)$, because the geometric fibres are orbits and $B$ is invariant. The pullback convention for $E_R$ is [lem-per-weil-divisor-strict-local-cartier-test].

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, printed p.125, Q-Cartier paragraph; VI 3.5(a), 3.7(a), printed pp.74–75, for the equivariant chart.

proof.text: Set $c=b^N\in R$. This element is nonzero, since $A$ is a domain, and is a non-zero-divisor in the subring $R$. For any prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, choose a prime $P$ of $A$ above it by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over]. Then $c\in\mathfrak p$ if and only if $b^N\in P$, if and only if $b\in P$. Thus $V_R(c)$ is exactly the image of $V_A(b)$, the strict-local image of $B$. This proves the last paragraph's Cartier equation and the asserted support. The next step controls coefficients rather than merely support.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, printed p.125, Q-Cartier paragraph; VI 3.5(a), 3.7(a), printed pp.74–75, for the equivariant chart.

proof.text: The height-one localizations of the Noetherian normal domains $R,A$ are DVRs by [lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel]. For $i\in S$ let $p_i=(t_i)\cap R$, choose a uniformizer $\pi_i\in R_{p_i}$, and put $e_i=v_{(t_i)}(\pi_i)>0$. The map $R_{p_i}\to A_{(t_i)}$ is local: a denominator outside $p_i$ is outside $(t_i)$. It sends units to units. Hence writing $z=u\pi_i^m$ proves $v_{(t_i)}(z)=e_i v_{p_i}(z)$ for every nonzero $z\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. Now put $f=\prod_{i\in S}t_i^{e_i}$ and $c_1=f^N\in R$, using the characters from Step 2. Its order at $(t_i)$ is $Ne_i$, and its order at every other height-one prime of $A$ is zero, by the prime factorization in [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization]. Every height-one prime of $R$ lifts by Step 3. The displayed valuation formula therefore gives $\operatorname{div}_R(c_1)=N E_R$: the coefficient is $N$ at every component of the image and zero elsewhere. Multiple branches over one prime give the same coefficient $N$.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, printed p.125, Q-Cartier paragraph; VI 3.5(a), 3.7(a), printed pp.74–75, for the equivariant chart.

proof.text: Let $M=|G|$. Partitioning $G$ into left $H$-cosets gives $M=kN$ for a positive integer $k$. Thus $c_1^k$ has divisor $M E_R$ at every strict local point. Apply [lem-per-weil-divisor-strict-local-cartier-test] to the fixed effective Weil divisor $E$ on the normal Noetherian scheme $Y$ and the single global integer $M$. It produces a global effective Cartier divisor $C$ with Weil divisor $ME$, support $D$, and single non-zero-divisor equations on pointed etale neighborhoods. In particular $E$ is effective Q-Cartier; in fact the reduced image divisor itself is Q-Cartier.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, printed p.125, Q-Cartier paragraph; VI 3.5(a), 3.7(a), printed pp.74–75, for the equivariant chart.

proof.text: Pull $C$ back along $h$. Locally its equation $c$ is nonzero on every generic component of $Y$. A birational modification identifies dense opens componentwise, so at every generic point of $Y'$ its pullback is still nonzero. At any point of regular $Y'$ the local ring is a domain; injecting it into the function field of that component shows the pulled-back equation is nonzero and hence a non-zero-divisor. Therefore $C'=h^*C$ is effective Cartier and has support $h^{-1}D$. Write $E'=(h^{-1}D)_{\rm red}$ and $F'=(h^{-1}q(\overline B))_{\rm red}$. The containment $E'\subseteq F'$ is set-theoretic; no claim of equality of nonreduced ideal sheaves is used.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, printed p.125, Q-Cartier paragraph; VI 3.5(a), 3.7(a), printed pp.74–75, for the equivariant chart.

proof.text: Use a normal-crossings etale chart at a point of $Y'$ [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor], where the ideal of $F'$ is $T=t_1\cdots t_r$. The chart local ring is regular by [lem-sfb-etale-stalk-invariants]. Let $c'$ be the equation of $C'$ there. Since $V(c')\subseteq V(T)$, some power $T^a$ belongs to $(c')$, so $c'$ is a unit after inverting $T$. By [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization], $c'=u\prod t_i^{n_i}$. Its radical ideal is generated by $\prod_{n_i>0}t_i$: these are pairwise nonassociate primes. By [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent] the pullback of $E'$ to the chart is the reduced induced subscheme on $V(c')$, so its ideal at $w$ is this radical, generated by a non-zero-divisor; a generator of the stalk generates the ideal, as a non-zero-divisor, on a neighbourhood of $w$. These charts cover $Y'$, so the same node makes $E'$ an effective Cartier divisor. Thus $E'$ has the required reduced parameter-product equation and is normal crossings. These equations show that every component of $E'$ is a codimension-one component of $F'$, including the empty-divisor case. If $F'$ is strict normal crossings, retain just those global components. Their intersections are among the regular intersections in [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], with the same codimension formula. Hence $E'$ is strict normal crossings as well.

source.place: VIII 5.3.8, printed p.125, Q-Cartier paragraph; VI 3.5(a), 3.7(a), printed pp.74–75, for the equivariant chart.
